_comment: Two different questions, kept apart on purpose. `measured` is reproducible with npm run survivorship and is what the site quotes. `endToEnd` is an older run whose method was never committed; it is kept because it may still be right about a question this cannot answer.

measured.question: Of the skill we measured, how much came from scoring names that were not in the index at the time?
measured.method: Spearman IC of the shipped tape scores against 21-day excess return, daily, then the same scores restricted to dated index membership. The model is NOT retrained — only the evaluation universe changes.
measured.lowerBoundReason: Dating membership removes companies that were not yet in the index. It cannot recover companies dropped after failing, because their prices were never fetched.

endToEnd.question: If the whole thing had been BUILT point-in-time — trained as well as evaluated — what would it be worth?
endToEnd.method: 15 CPCV arrangements with membership applied per row. Retrains on the filtered data, so it carries the cost of 20% fewer training rows as well as the harder universe.
endToEnd.note: Recorded in ENGINE_TODO.md from a run whose script was never committed. It cannot be re-derived, so it is not quoted on the site. Answering it properly is a training job.
